title: Annotator speeding and copy detection
scenario: Scan a day of captioning submissions: reject rows with bad timestamps, flag annotators whose share of sub-20-second submissions is at least 0.5, and flag annotators who gave the same normalised answer as a different annotator on a task.

verified.why_correct: `<` looks like a boundary slip, but the spec says under 20 seconds is fast and exactly 20 is not. ann-07's 20-second submission confirms it. The duration uses total_seconds(), not .seconds.
split()/join collapses every run of whitespace and trims the ends, lower() handles case, and rstrip('.!?') drops trailing punctuation, exactly as README rule 4 says.

bugs.title: Same annotator resubmitting counted as copying
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_annotator_table: ann-06 is flagged ['copying']. Test 2: copy_tasks gains 'T4': ['ann-06'] and ann-06 appears in flagged.
bugs.why: A list keeps one entry per submission, so ann-06 submitting the same answer twice on T4 makes len(who) == 2 although only one annotator is involved. The spec needs two different annotators.

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_report()?
context_qa.a: `load_registry` builds a set of normalised annotator ids from annotators.csv. `load_submissions` returns `(valid, rejected)`. build_report then builds one `AnnotatorReport` per annotator with valid submissions, counts fast ones with `timing.is_fast`, calls `flag_speeders`, and adds `copying` flags from `copying.copy_tasks`.

context_qa.q: Which rows does load_submissions skip before parsing timestamps?
context_qa.a: Rows whose annotator id (as computed in that function) is not in the registry set. Those rows are skipped without being parsed or recorded anywhere.
`parse_time` raises ValueError if a timestamp matches none of the three formats in `TIME_FORMATS`, and parse_submission raises ValueError itself when `submitted_at` is earlier than `started_at`.

It is a property on `AnnotatorReport` in models.py: `fast / submissions`, rounded to 3 decimals, or 0.0 if there are no submissions. `fast` is the count of submissions for which `is_fast` returned True.

It groups submissions by `(task_id, norm_answer(answer))`. For each group it builds `who` from the annotator ids, and when `who` has two or more entries those annotators are added to that task's set. It returns task id → sorted names, with tasks sorted.

context_qa.q: Which annotators appear in the report?
context_qa.a: Only annotators who have at least one valid (non-rejected) submission, since table rows are created while iterating over valid submissions. They are listed in sorted id order.
